clinician.trajectory_summary: A Japanese infant (36 weeks + 3 days, 1860g) with fetal growth restriction was prenatally diagnosed with severe symptomatic congenital CMV infection following maternal seroconversion (fever at 4 weeks gestation, positive CMV-IgG/IgM). At birth, congenital CMV was confirmed by positive CMV-DNA in urine and whole blood. Physical examination revealed hepatosplenomegaly, intravertebral calcification, and microcephaly. Ophthalmoscopic examination on admission (E001) demonstrated posterior vessel dilation, demarcation lines at the temporal peripheral zone bilaterally, and arteriovenous anastomosis in the right eye without active chorioretinitis. The diagnosis of ocular CMV infection was established by detection of CMV-DNA in aqueous humor via PCR (E003). Antiviral therapy with oral valganciclovir was initiated around day 5 of life, resulting in complete regression of vessel dilation and remarkable improvement of the arteriovenous anastomosis by day 11 (E004). At 3-month follow-up, fluorescein angiography showed near-complete regression of the anastomosis but revealed chorioretinal atrophy at the macula and around the optic disc (E005), consistent with ocular CMV sequelae.
